chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever deals with the people without oppressing them; and speaks to them without lying to them; and makes promises to them without breaking them, is one of those whose manliness (murū'ah) is complete; and his justice (adalat) has become apparent; and his brotherhood is obligatory, and his backbiting is forbidden.

key_terms.أُخُوَّةٌ: Brotherhood, referring to the social and spiritual bond between believers.
key_terms.عَدَالَةٌ: Justice or uprightness, indicating a person's reliability and moral standing.
key_terms.غِيْبَةٌ: Backbiting, the act of mentioning a person in their absence in a way they dislike.
key_terms.مُرُوَّةٌ: Manliness or moral integrity, a key concept in Shia ethics denoting noble character.

ai.seo_question: What are the three qualities that make a person's character complete and their backbiting forbidden in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* emphasizes that moral integrity (*murū'ah*) and justice (*'adālah*) are demonstrated through consistent social conduct: fairness, truthfulness, and reliability. In Shia tradition, these traits not only validate a person's character but also establish the sanctity of their honor, making backbiting (*ghībah*) a violation of the rights of a true brother in faith.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-34 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said,

“Whoever does not oppress the people when dealing with them, and does not lie to them when he talks with them is one whose manliness has been proven and his justness has become apparent. It is obligatory to treat him as a brother, and it is forbidden to gossip behind his back.”
